ov: Social insects living in colonies of a queen, workers and males, with more than 13,800 species described of an estimated 22,000. They live on almost every landmass on Earth.

why.et: Many human cultures use ants in food, medicine and rituals.
why.p: Mostly as ant farms, which were popular educational toys from the late 1950s to the late 1970s.

rg: Almost every landmass except Antarctica and a few remote islands; most abundant in moist tropical ecosystems.
df: Most species are omnivorous generalists, acting as herbivores, predators and scavengers; a few are specialists.

cf.tip: Termites live in colonies too, but they’re related to cockroaches, not ants.

fx: Ant queens can live up to 30 years, while workers live one to three.
Only queens and males have wings, and queens shed theirs after the mating flight.
